brief: Pale concrete stave silo about 14 ft across and 42 ft high, bound by thin steel hoops, capped by a ribbed galvanized-metal dome. An enclosed chute runs up the side where it meets the barn, and an open steel ladder scaffold stands against the back. It rises beside the stone lower wall of a big red-sided bank barn with a white-lettered gable end, a vegetable garden and wire fence in front, along a two-lane highway.

facade.notes: Lincoln Highway Farm (Schellsburg PA), HAER: a red bank barn with a white-trimmed gable and a long forebay along the highway, a pale concrete stave silo with a ribbed dome, a smaller crib, a white farmhouse beyond; a wire fence and the straight two-lane highway

why.note: the dairy farm's silo: concrete staves from c.1910, built against the barn's end so silage could be pitched down a chute into the feeding alley
the Pennsylvania bank barn, carried west across Ohio: built into a slope, the threshing floor entered from the bank, the stable below
